meta.title: Installation
meta.description: Bevel systems install via the shadcn CLI. Each system is copied directly into your project — no npm package, no versioning, no lock-in.

blocks.content: Bevel requires an existing Next.js project with shadcn/ui already configured. If you're starting fresh, set that up first.
Bevel is framework-agnostic at its core but the CLI tooling and import paths assume Next.js with the App Router. Remix and Vite support is on the roadmap.
If you haven't set up shadcn/ui yet, run the init command.
Each Bevel system installs independently. You only install what you need.

blocks.code:
# Product Tour
npx shadcn@latest add https://bevelui.vercel.app/r/tour.json

# Command Palette
npx shadcn@latest add https://bevelui.vercel.app/r/command-palette.json

# File Upload
npx shadcn@latest add https://bevelui.vercel.app/r/file-upload.json

# Form Engine
npx shadcn@latest add https://bevelui.vercel.app/r/form-engine.json

blocks.content: The CLI will install any required npm dependencies automatically and copy the component files into your project.
After installation, your project structure will look like this.
After installation, import from the same path the CLI created. The code snippets in these docs use the same paths — copy-paste safe.

blocks.title: Keep imports relative within each system
blocks.content: Internal imports between files within the same system use relative paths (./tour-context). Never use absolute paths inside the system files — they will break in the consumer's project.
